candidate_object: The exact six ordinary 2-blocks of the centerless simple group L4(3), explicit defect-group representatives with exponents 8,4,1,1,1,1, all 29 ordinary-character 2-defects, and the resulting Proposition 3.2 implication at the single prime 2 for nearly-simple triples with derived subgroup L4(3).

target_vs_witness.canonical_target: The full integer divisibility o(x)chi(1) divides |G| for every finite G, every ordinary irreducible complex chi, and every x with exact chi(x) nonzero.
target_vs_witness.bounded_claim: Condition (1.1) at the prime 2 for nearly-simple triples whose derived subgroup is exactly centerless L4(3), obtained from the verified 2-block exponent inequalities.

rows.candidate_value: The submitted proof claim explicitly quantifies only over the six 2-blocks of fixed L4(3), and Proposition 3.2 then over triples with derived subgroup L4(3); it does not claim the universal finite-group quantifier.
The fixed base group is the finite group PSL(4,3) of order 6065280, and the Proposition 3.2 corollary concerns finite nearly-simple groups H.
The block partition and all 29 defects use Irr(CharacterTable("L4(3)")), hence ordinary irreducible complex characters; Proposition 3.2 likewise uses ordinary Irr(H).
For the Proposition 3.2 implication, h is an element of finite H and o(hZ(H))_2 is its exact quotient-order 2-part; centerlessness gives the exact o(h)_2 statement.
The Proposition 3.2 implication is conditional on exact ordinary nonvanishing chi(h) != 0; this also forces irreducibility of chi restricted to the derived subgroup in the intended triple.
The proved conclusion is only o(h)_2 divides (|H|/chi(1))_2 for triples with derived subgroup L4(3); the full integer divisibility for arbitrary finite groups remains unanswered.
